reasoning_text:
Okay, let's see. I need to figure out which of these four Persian poetry couplets has a different concept or message from the others. First, I should understand what each one is saying.

Starting with option 1: "هنوز بر سر پیمان و عهد و سوگندم - اگر چه مهر بریدی و عهد بشکستی". Translating this, the first line says "I still have the covenant, pact, and oath on my head" and the second line is "Although you have broken the seal and the pact". So this seems to be about someone who is still holding onto their promises or oaths despite the other person breaking them. The message is about loyalty or keeping one's word even when others don't.

Option 2: "ما بر آن عهدیم و پیمان بی وفا پیداست کیست - بی وفاآن است کاو برگردد از پیمان دوست". The first part is "We are on that pact, and who is unfaithful to it?" The second line says "Unfaithful is he who turns back from the pact of a friend". This one is also talking about pacts and faithfulness, emphasizing that breaking a pact with a friend is unfaithful. The message is about the importance of keeping promises, especially with friends.

Option 3: "دشمن شوند و سر برود هم بر آن سریم - ما را سری است با تو که گر خلق روزگار". The first line: "They become enemies and leave, yet we still remain on that head". The second line: "Our head is with you, if the creation of the age is..." Hmm, maybe the second part is about the creation of the world or time. The message here seems to be about staying loyal even when others leave or become enemies, maintaining a connection or commitment despite external changes.

Option 4: "نشینم به رهش بر سر کویش نروم - مصلحت دیده چنین صبر که سویش نروم". Translating: "I will not sit in his shade, nor go to his courtyard. I have seen the benefit of such patience that I do not go towards him." This one is about not seeking shelter or associating with someone, perhaps due to past experiences or wisdom. The message is more about avoiding someone or a situation, maybe out of self-interest or having learned from past mistakes.

Comparing all options, 1, 2, and 3 are all about pacts, oaths, and loyalty, even when others break them. Option 4 is different because it's about avoiding someone rather than about keeping promises. So the outlier is option 4.
